Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not always easy - it often requires quite a lot of independence to find e.g. subjects and opportunities

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome programme

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy - it is quite expensive in Heidelberg and not easy to find an apartment by yourself, especially not in the center of the city. I wanted to have my own place so I found a small basement apartment on Airbnb 6 km from uni for 600€ pr. month and rented a bike and bought a semester bus/train-ticket.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can get a bit lonely, but if you are ok with that it is absolutely fine. I didn't have time to do very many social things anyway because the study required a lot of preparation and reading.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really look into it - I got some emails about applying for a room on campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Going on an exchange requires a lot of preparation and many processes. But in Germany, many things take place a little more slowly, as there is quite a lot of bureaucracy - you sometimes also have to push them for answers.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are contact persons

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It ended well, but it took a long time to find exciting subjects that matched the number of ECTS and weekly teaching hours. I had to make some changes along the way and ask for pre-approval while I was down there. The professors decide a lot in Germany and several suddenly decided to change the teaching hours, so I had to rearrange my schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take a good time for it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Interesting subjects - although I must say that the academic level is really high and not always suitable for law exchange students, especially not when not perfect in German language.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were only lectures - no classroom teaching. It therefore becomes quite lonely for exchange students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Einführung in die deutsche Rechtssprache
Handelsrecht
Grundkurs Strafrecht
Grundkurs Zivilrecht
GmbH-Recht
Vertragliche Schuldverhältnisse
Gewerblicher Rechtsschutz

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Handelsrecht and Gewerblicher Rechtsschutz
These are exciting legal subjects, but require good knowledge of German. Many of the rules are based on EU regulation and are therefore very similar to e.g. the Danish rules

questions.answer: Can't remember - nothing big

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books - you can borrow them at the library for free which is nice. But it is a good idea to buy the small handbook with BGB (German civil law codification) and other relevant rules for your subjects (e.g. StGB, HandelsG etc.) These cost like 10-15€ pr book.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use them but I know there were different opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, pub nights etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't have time to participate

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have time, go see the surrounding cities - Strasbourg is also only 2 hours away by bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not so difficult as I have lived in a German speaking country and know the culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: ELSA Heidelberg has different opportunities + the buddy/tandem-programme

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's a beautiful city and the people are also nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Speak fluent German
Choose subjects that remind you of some you have had in your home country
Be prepared that there is a greater distance between you and the professors than you are used to

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Great professional benefit and basic knowledge of the German legal system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A bureaucratic system and that you are left to your own devices in terms of learning (there is no concrete syllabus), you have to reach out yourself and you don't always get help, etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Try to find accommodation as close to the center of the city as possible - that would have made it a bit more fun for me.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
